title: Building a campus study-group app (mock data)
topic: A short interview about a study-group app that matches students by course and free time. The team explains the scheduling logic, how they handle cancellations, the ideal group size, and how timetable privacy is protected.

messages.speaker: S3
messages.text: Welcome everyone. Today we're talking about how students can build a study-group app. Priya, let's start with you.

messages.speaker: S1
messages.text: Thanks. The core idea is simple: match students who are taking the same course and have overlapping free time.

messages.speaker: S2
messages.text: From the engineering side, the hardest part was the scheduling logic. We use a greedy matcher first and optimize later.

messages.speaker: S3
messages.text: Rahul, how do you handle students who keep cancelling?

messages.speaker: S2
messages.text: We added a reliability score. If someone cancels late, their score drops and the matcher ranks them lower.

messages.speaker: S1
messages.text: We also found that groups of three or four work best. Larger groups tend to split into side conversations.

messages.speaker: S3
messages.text: What about privacy, since you collect timetables?

messages.speaker: S1
messages.text: Timetables stay on the device until a match is confirmed, and only the overlapping slots are shared.

messages.speaker: S2
messages.text: Next we want to add shared notes, and maybe a quiz generator built from the course material.

chapters.title: Introduction and core idea
chapters.summary: The host introduces the app; Priya explains matching by course and free time and Rahul describes the scheduling logic.

chapters.title: Cancellations and group size
chapters.summary: A reliability score ranks flaky users lower, and groups of three or four work best.

chapters.title: Privacy and next steps
chapters.summary: Timetables stay on-device until a match is confirmed. Next: shared notes and a quiz generator.

takeaways: Match students by shared course and overlapping free time.
A reliability score discourages late cancellations.
Groups of 3-4 work best; larger groups split up.
Timetables stay on-device until a match is confirmed.
Planned: shared notes and an auto quiz generator.
